notes:
This is an early build, released to consoles set to Latest Updates.

New systems: Master System and Sega CD tabs, both on Genesis Plus GX. Sega CD games go in as .chd, .cue and .bin, or .iso, and need the Sega CD BIOS for their region, uploaded on the web page under Files, BIOS. A game that is missing it names the file it needs.

Wii: a Wii game's page has Motion source. Tilt the console uses the Switch's own motion sensor for Wii Remote 1 in handheld, so the pointer works with the Joy-Cons on the rails. Wii pointer speed is now a slider from 70 to 150 percent. Settings, Controllers has Set dead zone by hand, and Calibrate control sticks now sees Bluetooth controllers.

Wii U: the web page's Saves tab takes your Wii U Mii file (FFL_ODB.dat, from Mii Maker's save) and puts it where Wii U games read it. network_services.xml goes in the Wii U online play box under Files, BIOS, and Custom is offered as a network.

Ports: Sly, Pokemon Colosseum and Black Ops II each have an Uninstall button on the web page, and your saves stay. Pokemon Colosseum builds v0.4.0, with the Wish crash and the move sound echo fixed. Press Build the update in its section on the web page; your save carries over. New Game now asks whether to start with Espeon and Umbreon.

Fixes: "Updated to" shows once the update has fully finished. The web page's Replace files prompt no longer opens behind the file browser. A PC game whose program is missing from its folder says so. The diagnostic logs show what is using the Wii system memory, and their CPU clock and 3DS motion sections print again.

Not yet tried with a real Master System or Sega CD game, with Miis inside a Wii U game, or with each tilt direction by hand. Reports welcome.

stable.notes:
The 2.41 changes, now on the Stable channel. If this console was on 2.40.0,
it also gets the whole 2.40 series, summed up at the end.

This update carries a new boot script: the console restarts once for the
update and once more on its own about a minute after the first boot. Do not
power off while it says part 2 of 2.

The SD card's fastest mode (DDR200) is now used on Samsung cards only, as
Switchroot does. Other cards run in the standard mode: if yours used the
fast mode, games load a little slower, but SanDisk cards, which cannot run
it reliably on the Switch, no longer get read errors under load. If a
Samsung card gives read errors, turn DDR200 off in the SCCM Retro app's Boot
settings.

The SCCM Retro app on the Homebrew menu is now one app: Launch SCCM Retro,
Launch in Safe Mode (stock clocks and voltages, once), Options (WiFi and
Bluetooth, boot settings, auto launch), and installing or removing SCCM
Retro on an SD card. The separate installer and calibration apps are
removed.

Swap A and B now applies only to Gen1Recomp and Moonlight, the two games
that offer it.

New background: Arcade, in Settings, Display and Sound, Appearance.

From 2.40.0, also: the console boots in about 28 seconds instead of about
50; Ocarina of Time and Majora's Mask, and Mario Kart Wii as a native port
with Retro Rewind online, on Ports and Apps; a PC Games tab for Windows
games; auto save for RetroArch, 3DS and PS2 games; Wii U, GameCube, WiFi
and volume button fixes; and a security fix to install permissions.
